subject: docs/coop/artifacts/route-b.DR-011.preview-disposition.v2.json
summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. DR-011 is the row with sixteen residuals underneath it, so the failure mode is a parent disposition that quietly absorbs them. This one does the opposite: it enumerates all sixteen by id, then enumerates them a second time in whatMustNotBePretendedSettled with a description each, and I checked every one of those descriptions against its own file 08 row. All sixteen correspond. The R03 handling is the sharpest case and it is right at source — file 08's own needs cell for R03 says 'do not infer acceptance from execution alone', which is exactly the principle this disposition applies when it refuses to read check-c2-v12's ACCEPT-STANDING as residual closure. rowQuoted is faithful, all three digests and both commits verify, and the register-state premises are true in the post-D-081 file 08.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 646957f467322327e7b54cc6d1462a8685bfa79dfb9c9e3920cff93a4532bc81, equal to the dispatch-supplied and prompt-stated value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. I verified the prompt against the dispatch digest 98eb5495… before relying on it.

The attack 'closes or reclassifies any residual R01–R16' fails, and I tested the sixteen-item map rather than the refusal language. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled names every residual with a description, and each description corresponds to its file 08 row: R01 FACT-PLANE subject-set/sufficiency view, R02 FACT-IDENTITY capability property, R03 the C2 effective-checker line, R04 DELIVERY OBS-1, R05 Rust provider PC-7, R06 EVIDENCE validator-standing and joins, R07 retention checker standing and the D9/EVIDENCE join, R08 D9 R-V114-F1/F2 plus three contract gaps, R09 R-1 CIR-B1 and identity parks, R10 R2-FINAL-03 blind litmus, R11 OPERABILITY G19, R12 evaluation-proof dual-head, R13 VERSIONING stale D9/RC-14, R14 RESOLVED-INPUTS CFG-6, R15 TRUSTED-REQUEST-CONTEXT identity recipes, R16 the P-1/P-2/G3 product-boundary successor. Nothing is omitted and nothing is described as another residual.

The R06 and R07 descriptions are scoped to exactly the un-closed halves, which is the detail a careless parent disposition would flatten. file 08 records both as 'NARROWED — application half closed, validator-standing and join halves OPEN' and '…checker-standing and join halves OPEN'; the disposition names 'EVIDENCE validator-standing and joins' and 'Retention checker standing and D9/EVIDENCE join' — the remaining halves only, not the closed application halves.

The attack 'treats check-c2-v12 ACCEPT-STANDING as R03 CLOSED' fails on three surfaces and is correct at source. whatMustNotBePretendedSettled reads 'C2 effective-checker live-tree green (R03; check-c2-v12 ACCEPT-STANDING is standing, not residual CLOSED)'; whatThisDoesNotDo repeats 'Does not treat check-c2-v12 ACCEPT-STANDING as R03 CLOSED'; and P-011-1's bound forbids treating 'a green checker, an ACCEPT-STANDING instrument review, or this parent disposition as residual closure'. file 08's R03 row describes 'a checker-review/subject-standing mismatch' and its needs cell instructs 'Pin the effective checker and its independent standing or record a V1-owned alternative; do not infer acceptance from execution alone.' The disposition is applying file 08's own rule, not inventing a caution.

rowQuoted is faithful. The decision text and the owner string both match file 08's DR-011 row exactly; statusAtAuthoring HARD-BLOCKED matches its leading label; and blueprintImpact is identical to the register's cell once markdown backticks around SATISFIED are set aside — I diffed the two strings and the only difference is two backtick characters.

The register-state premises are true against the post-D-081 file 08. The d070Note says 'D-070 and D-081 appended preview-scope notes to nine other rows. DR-011 still has no scoped owner-recorded disposition.' Exactly nine rows carry a preview-scope note — DR-002 through DR-010, one each — and DR-011 carries none. The same note's status formulation, 'Residuals R01-R16 remain individually OPEN, NARROWED, or otherwise not CLOSED', matches my own row-by-row reading: fourteen OPEN, two NARROWED, none CLOSED.

Examined and cleared: the field named residualsRemainOpen lists all sixteen ids, including R06 and R07 whose row-level status token is NARROWED rather than OPEN. I followed this down rather than filing it, because this corpus treats status tokens as load-bearing. It resolves in the document's favour on three grounds — file 08 itself describes those two rows' remaining halves as 'halves OPEN', so nothing is misstated about their substance; the same document states the precise 'OPEN, NARROWED, or otherwise not CLOSED' formulation in d070Note; and the per-residual descriptions scope R06 and R07 to their open halves only. The field's operative content, which residuals are not closed, is accurate for all sixteen.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails, with an addition specific to this row. ownerWhoMustRecord reads 'V1 coordinator and each surface owner (file 08 DR-011). Coordinator may draft a parent-row disposition. D-000 does not make the coordinator those surface owners. A coordinator-composed residual CLOSED is unlawful.' That last sentence extends DR-204's rule from SATISFIED to residual closure, which is the guard a sixteen-residual parent needs. condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded adds 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording and is not residual CLOSED' — foreclosing my own verdict from being read either way.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW; the condition-1 effect is scoped to 'the DR-011 parent within architecture-preview scope only. Residuals stay OPEN'; and honesty concedes 'File 08 still forbids SATISFIED of DR-011 while any residual is OPEN', which matches the register's acceptance cell requiring every residual CLOSED or LAWFULLY-DISPOSED.

whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA is honest about the shape of the remaining work rather than reducible to a checklist: individual CLOSED or LAWFULLY-DISPOSED evidence for every residual, R10 after all surface adjudications and V10 resolution, and parent SATISFIED only after residuals close or are lawfully disposed. The R10-last ordering matches COORD's 'R10 the final blind consumer-B litmus — structurally LAST'.

The attacks 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' and 'file 08 edited' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses both, condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded preserves condition 5 as the only authorization for that directory, file 08 measures at its cited digest, and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

The selection authority is real and correctly characterised: D-055 is ADOPTED at commit 5acba0fe4660cbb5aace6b535585151f774422f9, which resolves to 'D-055: select Route B for DR-011 parent (preview scope)', and the artifact states that selection 'Writes no disposition. This artifact is that later disposition draft.' whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not re-adopt or overturn D-055.'

All cited digests match live bytes: COORD d93614cd…, file 08 1360a4f8… at its post-D-081 value, and the v1 predecessor at 133ae334…. The D-081 commit b1885620… resolves to 'D-081: file-08 notes for DR-006/007/009 owner recordings'. predecessorChange scopes the delta honestly: 'Retargets selection authority from unadopted D-055 draft to adopted D-055. Refreshes live pins after D-081. Does not close residuals.'
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of prompt and subject three times at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions, checking the prompt against the dispatch digest first; digest verification of COORD, file 08 and the v1 predecessor against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for the D-055 and D-081 commits; automated token-overlap comparison of each of the sixteen whatMustNotBePretendedSettled residual descriptions against its own file 08 row, followed by manual inspection of the one the tokenizer flagged (R03, a hyphenation artifact); per-row status extraction of all sixteen residual rows with OPEN/NARROWED/CLOSED tallies; extraction of the R06 and R07 NARROWED clauses to test whether the descriptions scope to the open halves; string-equality comparison of rowQuoted decision, owner and blueprintImpact against the live DR-011 row with a character diff on the last; count of preview-scope notes across DR-002..DR-011 to test the nine-rows claim; json field checks of status, binds, sealRecommendation, reviewStatus, the whatThisDoesNotDo entries and the coordinator-authority sentences; git status across docs/v2/architecture

acceptNote: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories. A parent disposition sitting above sixteen residuals is the easiest place in this corpus to absorb work that has not been done, and this one is built the other way round: it lists the sixteen twice, once as bare ids and once with a description each, and every description lands on its own file 08 row. The R03 case is the one I expected to find loose, since an ACCEPT-STANDING instrument review is exactly the thing a drafter might lean on, and instead the disposition applies file 08's own instruction not to infer acceptance from execution alone. I record explicitly that I probed one thing and let it go: the field named residualsRemainOpen includes R06 and R07, whose row status is NARROWED. I followed it to file 08, which itself calls those rows' remaining halves OPEN, and to the same document's precise formulation elsewhere — it resolves in the artifact's favour, so I am reporting none rather than padding.
